The Digital Product Passport (DPP) supports sharing product and process information among supply-chain businesses, authorities, and consumers. It improves transparency and information transfer for circular product design, manufacturing, regulatory monitoring, and enforcement. The DPP can include information about components, materials, chemical substances, reparability, spare parts, environmental impact, and professional end-of-life disposal. This data model is expected to evolve with the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation and related delegated acts.

The Product Footprint Entity with sustainability information such as the different environmental footprint types, the carbon and material footprint explicitly, applicable rules and lifecycle stages.

Quantification of the product's environmental impacts throughout its life cycle, for one or more impact categories or an aggregated set of categories. The value may be based on the Product Environmental Footprint method established by Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279 or another applicable scientific method adopted through Union legislation. Related product-performance information may include environmental-footprint, carbon-footprint, durability, or reparability indicators.

The carbon footprint of the product. This is mentioned in the ESPR provisional agreement from January 9th, 2024 Annex I:
The following parameters shall, as appropriate, and where necessary supplemented by others, be used, individually or combined, as a basis for improving the product aspects referred to in Article 5(1):
(m) the carbon footprint of the product;
and Article 7:
(2)(b)(i) information on the performance of the product in relation to one or more of the product parameters referred to in Annex I, including a scoring of reparability or durability, carbon footprint or environmental footprint;
and defined by Article 2:
(25) 'carbon footprint' means the sum of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and GHG removals in a product system, expressed as CO2 equivalents and based on a life cycle assessment using the single impact category of climate change.

The material footprint of the product. This is mentioned in the ESPR provisional agreement from January 9th, 2024 Annex I:
(ma) the material footprint of the product;
and defined by Article 2:
(25a) 'material footprint' refers to the total amount of raw materials extracted to meet final consumption demands.

Applicable product documentation, including declarations of conformity, technical documentation, conformity certificates, user manuals, instructions, warnings, and safety information. Digital instructions should support assembly, installation, operation, storage, maintenance, repair, refurbishment, remanufacture, disassembly, reuse, recycling, and end-of-life disposal where relevant. Documentation may also cover product-data access, required tools and skills, compatibility, precautions, and the separation, reuse, recycling, or disposal of packaging materials.

Data in form of open fields which need to be transferred in addition. The regulation is still under development and may change in the future. To accommodate this, additional data allows the option to include additional data required by future changes to the regulation. In addition, the DPP can be easily updated and adapted to the new requirements. 
The ESPR provisional agreement from January 9th, 2024 Article 9 mentions:
2. Where other Union legislation requires or allows the inclusion of specific information in the product passport, that information may be included in the product passport pursuant to the applicable delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 4.

Generic current-state submodel describing the product's present position and status in manufacturing, supply, use, service, remanufacturing and circular value chains. It exposes current ownership, responsibility, status, whereabouts and product evidence. Snapshot versioning, timestamps, ownership of exchanged snapshots and historical reconstruction are managed transparently by the Data Space and traceability application. Workflow and process execution information belongs in separate Process or Manufacturing Lifecycle Digital Twins.
